cap: Progesterone raises ventilatory drive, so tidal volume rises 30 to 40 percent while respiratory rate barely changes. Ventilation outruns the 20 percent rise in oxygen consumption, so PaCO2 falls to about 30 mm Hg and the kidney lowers bicarbonate: a compensated respiratory alkalosis. The raised diaphragm lowers FRC and residual volume, but total lung capacity stays nearly the same.
teach: Read each cause against its effect. The hormonal cause explains the gas result, the metabolic cause explains why the lungs overshoot, and the structural cause explains the volumes. In pregnancy PaCO2 is about 30 mm Hg, so a value of 40 mm Hg means the patient is retaining carbon dioxide and may be tiring. The low FRC and high oxygen consumption leave little reserve, so a pregnant patient desaturates within seconds of apnea. Minute ventilation is tidal volume times rate, so it rises mostly through tidal volume.
